Two neighbouring properties are kept apart from it: execution impedance (does the step add time or cost?) and intervention opportunity (can another party bring an objection that changes the process?). A standing limit enforced by another's mechanism is a gate without impedance and need not be an opportunity; a rubber-stamp approval is a gate with impedance and no real opportunity; a channel for challenging a process's rules can be an opportunity without gating ordinary execution.
